# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

1846	## Acceptance Criteria
1847	
1848	*All criteria are GIVEN / WHEN / THEN and ids are `AC-IW-n` (the numbering was kept stable through the QA review, so the groups below are by topic, not contiguous). **Tags.** (auto) an automated test, logic in `tests/unit/instruments/`, integration in `tests/integration/instruments/`; (lint) a build or content lint (instrument data, scene tree, sheets, scripts); (review) a design or lead review of a document or a retained screenshot; (manual) a playtest or a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`; (spike) a time-boxed engine test whose result may change the design. `(provisional — X)` marks a criterion that depends on a neighbour still being written or a reply owed. **Test-evidence gate.** This is a UI plus Visual / Feel system: every criterion that cites a retained screenshot (AC-IW-5, 9, 25, 29, 48, 100 and the screenshot legs of 1 and 6) is BLOCKING at every `qa.level` including `minimal` (coding standards: a parse check is not a run); Logic criteria (D.1 to D.6, D.8 to D.12, IW-5, IW-11 to IW-14, IW-17, IW-19, IW-21, IW-24) need files in `tests/unit/instruments/`; the card joins with the Filter, Interaction and the Controller are Integration. **No criterion asserts that the indicative IW-29 manifest passes floor (i)** (advisor ruling R17). **Conventions fixed for every vector:** `round` is half away from zero, a "rolling second" is [t, t + 1000 ms), and a **tip-pixel flip** is a frame whose rounded tip coordinate differs from the previous frame's (Formulas intro, D.3, VA-6).*
1849	
1850	**Conventions for the criteria below** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. (1) **Latency oracle.** One convention for AC-IW-33, AC-IW-91 and AC-IW-114: a latency is counted in render frames at a fixed 60 Hz test clock between the frame in which the Adapter receives the cause and the first frame whose draw list reflects it. "Closed in the same render frame" means the instrument's probe `is_card_open()` reads false (and the card root's `visible` is false) by the end of that frame's `_process`; Godot's `queue_free()` runs at the end of the frame, so the test asserts the probe in the same frame and `is_instance_valid(card)` false at the start of the next frame, and never asserts node validity inside the frame of the cause. "Opens on the next render frame" means `is_card_open()` reads true at the end of the frame after the press. (2) **Seeds.** Every randomised test takes its seeds from a fixed list in the test data and prints them; no wall clock, no unseeded RNG. (3) **Machine.** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12, which closes X14 and supersedes R11)* A performance criterion is gated on the two reference machines at the spike: RM-DESKTOP (Windows 10/11 64-bit; 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; GPU of the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / AMD Radeon RX 570 4 GB class, Vulkan 1.2+; SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz; P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms) and RM-DECK (Steam Deck LCD 2022, SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz panel, 30 fps target; P99 ceiling 33.3 ms); `project.yaml` `qa.min_spec` records both. Every wall-clock figure is taken on a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus`, vsync on, after the pipeline's 120-frame warm-up, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded with each result; a pass needs P99 at most 90 % of the ceiling (headroom at least 1.7 ms desktop, 3.3 ms Deck). A figure not yet measured is "pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK", not blocked. The CI runner (its description recorded in the output) and the developer's machine give indicative figures only. (4) **Playtest coding rule.** For every (manual) playtest criterion the protocol is a scripted session, the observed statement is the tester's first unprompted explanation, it is coded by two coders against the criterion's word list (or the codes named in the criterion), a disagreement is settled by the producer, and the raw codes are retained in `production/qa/evidence/`.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

### H. Engine, performance and spikes

- **AC-IW-53** (auto) [UI-4, 4.6 dual focus]: GIVEN every instrument and card `Control`, WHEN enumerated recursively, THEN `mouse_filter` is IGNORE and `focus_mode` is NONE in `gameplay` and in `inspect_card`; hovering the card changes nothing.
- **AC-IW-54** (spike) [IW-10, OQ-IW-7]: GIVEN `Sprite2D` rotation versus pre-rotated frames under NEAREST at `k` 1 to 8 for needles of 18 and 24 px, WHEN swept from -120 to +120 degrees in 0.5-degree steps, THEN the rendered needle is one 8-connected pixel run from pivot to tip with no gap and a perpendicular thickness of 2 art px (a measured 3 on diagonals fails unless the ADR accepts it); otherwise the recorded fallback (a pre-rendered needle strip) applies.
- **AC-IW-55** (spike, **BLOCKED until the technical-director accepts or replaces the OQ-IW-10 number**) [OQ-IW-10, IW-12, IW-16] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: GIVEN 20 on-screen instruments with 4 lying, WHEN the presenter pass runs for 600 frames on RM-DESKTOP and on RM-DECK in the R12 build (release export, `forward_plus`, vsync on, 120-frame warm-up, startup read-back recorded; pending spike measurement; a CI-runner run is indicative only and its description is recorded in the output) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*, THEN the median and 99th-percentile frame cost are recorded and pass iff the median is at most 0.25 ms and the p99 at most 0.5 ms (the proposal, half of the Filter's `CPU_BUDGET_MS` 0.5 median; the technical-director may replace it and the criterion then reads against that number); the per-frame work is O(1) per instrument (D.1, D.4, D.5, D.11), the predicate subject lists are precomputed at section load (IW-12), and `perceived()` calls equal the on-screen instrument count (AC-IW-62); instrument draw calls are at most 2 per on-screen instrument (face and needle) plus 1 per lying instrument when the gleam fallback is active; the ShaderMaterial count added by instruments is 0 on the per-instance path and 0 on the fallback path, never above the LO-13 five.
- **AC-IW-56** (spike) [IW-14, OQ-IW-14]: GIVEN the bitmap instrument face, WHEN rendered at integer `H`, THEN all digits 0-9 advance equally (tabular), the zero is slashed, and `1`, `l` and `I` are pixel-distinct (ART 7.1 asset test); the locale list of AC-IW-88 either has a face or ships no card.

### I. Cross-system and process

- **AC-IW-105** (lint, routed to the accessibility-specialist next to OQ-IW-13) [IW-20, P4 "at least one channel of truth"]: GIVEN every lie-eligible LINEAR instrument in the manifest and its placement, WHEN linted, THEN a hue-independent TRUTH witness (the pipe flow pattern or the puddle) lies within `WITNESS_HOPS_MAX` of it, so the colour-blind Power-vs-Fuel backup is not left with the lying glass alone; a LINEAR instrument without one is TRUTH-default.
- **AC-IW-106** (review, plus auto at the producer's cross-check) [IW-12, IW-36, P2]: GIVEN each stress source in the IW-12 predicate (i)-(iii), WHEN checked against Adaptive Audio and Failure & Trail, THEN each has a sound tell or a world-witness tell owned there, and in a capture at `k` 1 with the instrument off-screen or its tremor sub-perceptible the tell still reaches the player, so zooming out never removes the 10-30 s warning; a source with only an instrument tremor fails.
- **AC-IW-108** (lint, plus review) [IW-29, OQ-SN-11, SN D.12] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; BLOCKING 1)*: GIVEN a **test-owned fixture manifest** (a data file under `tests/`, not the indicative table) whose rows carry `comfort_credit` and `alarm_credit` in {FIXED, SCANNER, SUIT_IN_ROOM, NONE} and a lint input `seat_scanner_usable` in {true, false}, WHEN the floor lints run, THEN (a) a SCANNER-only row counts for `seat_scanner_usable` true and not for false; (b) a FIXED row counts for both; (c) a SUIT_IN_ROOM credit counts only for an ALARM-direction lie, only when `mount_room` equals `subject_room`, and never for a COMFORT-direction lie nor for a REMOTE row; (d) a GLYPH never counts as another instrument's fixed partner; (e) per-site counts are reported as the pair `[count(false), count(true)]` and a site whose upper end is below 3 fails advisory floor (ii) while a site whose lower end is below 3 emits a finding; (f) for the indicative manifest as a regression input the reported ranges are home [3, 9], A [0, 4], B [1, 5], and the lint reports no `AT-FLOOR` tag for any site. The two P0 asks (a second `p_o2` dial in derelict A and in derelict B) are recorded as findings, not as passes. No criterion asserts that the indicative manifest as listed passes floor (i).
- **AC-IW-57** (review) [K-1 to K-18, X-3, X-4]: GIVEN this GDD, WHEN reviewed, THEN each carried conflict has a numbered handling, an owner and a route in X-4, every refresh owed to a neighbour is in X-3, and the neighbour GDDs that name this system (Filter, Interaction, Controller, Boarding, Item DB, Derelict Authoring, Emitter State, Lighting, Graph, Chart Table, HUD, Debug Overlay) have each been re-read against the rows in Interactions I-D after they land.
- **AC-IW-58** (lint) [reflexion log]: GIVEN this GDD, WHEN the stale-token list of X-3 (copied into `tools/ci/stale_tokens.txt`) is grepped, THEN it returns no hit outside a rejection, citation or withdrawal line.
- **AC-IW-61** (review) [K-2]: GIVEN the Pipeline owner, WHEN K-2 is raised, THEN the settle exemption (one triple plus the local scalars `prev_honest_pm`, `rest_pm`, the window step and the dwell candidate, closed form, never persisted, cleared and snapped on restore *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*) is acknowledged in an ADR or the conflict is escalated to the technical-director.

One criterion per requirement of those three sections that is not already carried above (the settle window and tremor onset are AC-IW-16 and AC-IW-20; zones are AC-IW-24; the dead frame is AC-IW-42; the forbidden surfaces are AC-IW-1).

- **AC-IW-90** (manual, playtest) [Game Feel "Feel Acceptance Criteria" 1]: GIVEN at least 6 first-session players and no prompting, WHEN asked to describe what they saw after a session with one honest, one tremoring and one lying gauge, THEN at least 4 of 6 describe the honest needle as "settling", "stepping" or "catching up", the lying one as "wandering", "drifting" or "won't settle", and the tremor as "shaking" (shared sample with AC-IW-52).
